\chapter{Not at All, Is That So?}
\label{ch:ta-not-at-all}
\hlchaptermodality{96}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say not at all, react with is that so and really, agree that's right, and say I don't know.}

\section[illavē illai]{\ta{இல்லவே} \ta{இல்லை} (illavē illai) — not at all}

\label{lesson:TA-C96-notatall}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for not yet, then the Tamil for the same.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{இல்லவே} \ta{இல்லை}}
\textbf{\ta{இல்லவே} \ta{இல்லை}} (\emph{illavē illai}) — \textquotedblleft{}not at all\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\ta{இல்லை}} said twice, the first time with the \textbf{-\ta{ஏ}} that says \emph{exactly}: no, and no again.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The strongest no.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{illavē illai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{illavē illai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{illavē illai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for not yet, then the Tamil for the same, then say \emph{illavē illai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{இல்லவே} \ta{இல்லை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Not at all\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[appaṭiyā?]{\ta{அப்படியா}? (appaṭiyā?) — is that so?}

\label{lesson:TA-C96-isthatso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for the same, then the Tamil for not at all.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அப்படியா}?}
\textbf{\ta{அப்படியா}?} (\emph{appaṭiyā?}) — \textquotedblleft{}is that so?\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}oh, really?\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{அப்படி}} is \textquotedblleft{}like that\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{-\ta{ஆ}} makes it a question.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to show you are listening.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{appaṭiyā?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{appaṭiyā?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{appaṭiyā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for the same, then the Tamil for not at all, then say \emph{appaṭiyā?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{அப்படியா}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Is that so?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[aṭaṭā]{\ta{அடடா} (aṭaṭā) — oh dear!, wow!}

\label{lesson:TA-C96-adada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for not at all, then the Tamil for is that so.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அடடா}}
\textbf{\ta{அடடா}} (\emph{aṭaṭā}) — \textquotedblleft{}oh dear!\textquotedblright{}, or \textquotedblleft{}wow!\textquotedblright{}, by tone.

Said to bad news it is sympathy; said to good news it is delight. \textbf{\ta{அடடா}, \ta{அப்படியா}?} — \textquotedblleft{}oh dear, is that so?\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A cry of surprise that can go either way.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭaṭā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭaṭā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{aṭaṭā!}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for not at all, then the Tamil for is that so, then say \emph{aṭaṭā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{அடடா} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Oh dear!, wow!\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[caritāṉ]{\ta{சரிதான்} (caritāṉ) — that's right}

\label{lesson:TA-C96-thatsright}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for is that so, then the Tamil for oh dear.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சரிதான்}}
\textbf{\ta{சரிதான்}} (\emph{caritāṉ}) — \textquotedblleft{}that's right\textquotedblright{}, \textquotedblleft{}quite so\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{சரி}} with \textbf{-\ta{தான்}}, \textquotedblleft{}that and no other\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Agreement.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{caritāṉ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{caritāṉ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{caritāṉ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for is that so, then the Tamil for oh dear, then say \emph{caritāṉ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சரிதான்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}That's right\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[teriyātu]{\ta{தெரியாது} (teriyātu) — (I) don't know}

\label{lesson:TA-C96-dontknow}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for oh dear, then the Tamil for that's right.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{தெரியாது}}
\textbf{\ta{தெரியாது}} (\emph{teriyātu}) — \textquotedblleft{}don't know\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{எனக்குத்} \ta{தெரியாது}} — \textquotedblleft{}I don't know\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}to me it is not known\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Not at all, is that so, oh dear, that's right, I don't know.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{teriyātu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{teriyātu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{eṉakkut teriyātu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for oh dear, then the Tamil for that's right, then say \emph{teriyātu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{தெரியாது} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}(I) don't know\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
